content.comment_body: Hello, I need to connect 55 [product_name] modules via Ethernet and access their data in a central [product_name] for monitoring. I also want to send setpoints from the HMI in the control room. I'm unsure how to set this up. Thank you.

Hello, based on my knowledge, if connecting all modules directly is not required, you can create subnetworks of up to 16 [product_name] modules using routers and then link them to the main PC. This approach is somewhat more complex and costly, but it should function properly.

Hello, if you do not use an additional PC, your HMI needs to support a separate connection for each [product_name] module. If that's not feasible, you should transfer the required data to as many [product_name] modules as the HMI can access, and then forward information between these modules. Alternatively, collect all necessary data in the [product_name] modules that your HMI supports, so the HMI can read from those accessible modules. For example, if your HMI communicates with only one [product_name] module: To write, go from HMI to a single module and forward the data to others. To read, gather data from all modules into one collector module, then let the HMI read from it. Hope this helps.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users are discussing how to connect and exchange data between 55 [product_name] modules over Ethernet for centralized monitoring. There is confusion about network architecture options, HMI connection limitations, and the need for additional devices such as routers or computers. Members are seeking ways to efficiently manage data transfer given the system constraints.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants a straightforward way to connect all 55 [product_name] modules via Ethernet, monitor their data centrally, and send setpoints from the HMI, preferably without complex configuration or significant extra hardware.
